synopsis: The capability plan should explain its fit with the Machinery Regulation from 20 January 2027, including possible notified-body assessment for machine-learning safety components [f10236]. The final plan should identify governing rules, applicability sign-off, whether simulation is accepted, relevant Machinery Regulation, PLD and AI Act dates, and an assessor engagement plan [f10165]. Simulation evidence should trace each claimed output to its supporting requirement or hazard and the final pass/fail argument under the Machinery Regulation and ISO 19014 performance levels [f8029]. The regulatory route remains uncertain until notified-body and counsel pre-consultation tests Annex I Part A applicability and simulation-evidence acceptability; no notified-body pre-consultation by early 2027, or ML perception without an Annex I Part A position, are warning signs [f10960, f10786]. The product liability lawyer expects a notified-body or legal opinion on Machinery Regulation and AI Act applicability, while EU-OSHA is cited only as an information agency summarizing the regulation, not as a regulator [f11134, f15686].
